title: AI Governance Lead

title: Lead Director - AI Governance Engineering
description: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Position Summary AI adoption across the organization is accelerating, and existing governance processes can add cycle time and rely heavily on manual review. We are building an AI Governance Engineering capability to modernize governance through automation—shifting from approval-heavy workflows to registration-driven workflows with built-in controls, and continuous observability. As Lead Director, AI Governance Engineering, you will create and lead a lean engineering team responsible for delivering governance-as-code: platform-agnostic SDKs, APIs, and automated controls that help teams move faster while ensuring responsible AI guardrails are consistently enforced. Key Responsibilities Automated Use Case Intake & Risk Classification Design unified intake APIs and user experiences that reduce friction and automatically populate metadata and integrate with application registration and provisioning workflows Implement dynamic intake flows for ML, Generative AI, and agentic use cases. Deliver automated inherent risk scoring and risk-based routing to provisioning and monitoring workflows. Governance-as-Code Toolkits Partner with AI Governance Data Scient to develop a platform-agnostic Python/SDK offering automated governance controls such as bias, drift, and AI safety testing. Integrate governance checks into CI/CD pipelines so evidence is generated during development. Enterprise Model & Use Case Registry Integration Enable event-driven ingestion of intake data and model artifacts into the enterprise registry. Support automated generation of audit-ready compliance artifacts and APIs for reviewers and auditors. Self-Service Enablement & Automation Expand policy-based routing for low- and high-risk AI use cases. Automate proof-of-concept lifecycle patterns and accelerate access to approved AI environments. Governance for Agentic Automation Establish execution safety patterns for internal AI agents, including permission-scoped actions. Partner with information security to implement runtime guardrails such as prompt filtering, data protection controls, and real-time observability. Leadership & Collaboration Build and lead a small, high-impact AI Governance Engineering team. Partner with AI platform teams, governance, security, and privacy partners to embed technical controls into development workflows. Define and track outcomes such as reduced intake complexity, faster cycle times, and improved governance transparency. Required Qualifications Experience leading software or platform engineering teams. Strong system architecture skills across APIs, automation, CI/CD, and data platforms. Experience building developer-facing tools such as SDKs, templates, or automation frameworks. Familiarity with ML and Generative AI lifecycles and how governance controls can be validated through automation. Ability to translate governance or risk requirements into scalable technical solutions. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Responsible AI concepts such as fairness, transparency, explainability, and auditability. Experience integrating automated quality gates into Git-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines. Background working in regulated or high-trust technology environments. Education Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Analytics, Engineering, or related discipline. Master's degree preferred What Success Looks Like AI intake processes are simpler, faster, and largely automated. Engineering teams have reusable SDKs and templates that make responsible AI the default. Validation of controls shifts from self-reporting to automated checks and evidence. Centralized observability provides real-time insight into AI usage, performance, and risk. If you are excited about building trusted AI systems through practical engineering, we encourage you to apply—even if you do not meet every qualification listed. We value collaboration, learning, and curiosity. title: Research Counsel

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. You'll be a subject matter expert on copyright, privacy, data use, and AI regulation (including the EU AI Act, U.S. state laws, and emerging global rules), and will work directly with researchers on questions that often have no settled answer. The ideal candidate will have navigated complex legal questions at the intersection of machine learning, data, and academic research in a fast-moving technical environment, with the judgment to work at the cutting edge of AI development while effectively solving issues, enabling innovation, and calibrating risk. This is a uniquely positioned role touching many different facets of AI, presenting the opportunity to be a leader in AI legal thought.  Key responsibilities Advise research and data teams on data sourcing, licensing, partnerships, and use, and help shape Anthropic's data acquisition and use strategy as laws and markets evolve Help coordinate regulatory readiness and model launches, review and chemical risk, including capability evaluations, tiered access for biosecurity researchers, and dual-use research questions Counsel the Societal Impacts, Economic, Alignment, Interpretability, Model Welfare, and Beneficial Deployments teams on research design, data collection and sharing, external collaborations, program launches, and publication review Monitor global AI, privacy, copyright, and export-control developments and translate them into practical internal guidance and policy, working closely with Product, Policy, and other legal stakeholders Engage with academics, regulators, industry groups, and civil society to help develop norms and best practices for responsible AI development and data governance Minimum qualifications A JD and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar (California or New York preferred) Practical, creative problem-solving: the ability to apply legal requirements to fast-changing, deeply technical work, with an understanding that the goal is to enable responsible research and product development in a risk-calibrated environment Exceptional communication and analytical skills, technical fluency, and the ability to navigate ambiguous and uncharted legal territory, turning complex technical and legal analysis into advice people can act on Familiarity and comfort advising on the EU AI Act, U.S. legislation and AI frameworks, GDPR/CCPA, and comparable regimes globally, sometimes where no AI-specific legislation exists Interest in thinking deeply about the impact of AI on society and how to make humanity's transition to the AI age as beneficial as possible Sound judgment about when to be flexible and when to hold a line; comfort making high-stakes calls in unsettled areas and outside your core expertise; and a low-ego, collaborative approach, doing the work needed rather than delegating it or being territorial Preferred qualifications At least 8 years of legal experience advising technology companies on copyright, privacy, data, AI regulation, and related product and policy issues, ideally including time in-house and work on AI/ML products or services Experience engaging directly with regulators or standards bodies Working technical literacy: enough familiarity with how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed to ask researchers and engineers the right questions and spot the legal issues in a technical design An academic or publishing background, or experience with copyright, open-source, and data licensing Experience with biosecurity, dual-use research, export controls, or safety frameworks such as Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy Experience advising on academic or industry research, including publications, external collaborations, data sharing, or title: Senior Strategist, Data & AI (Remote - US, UK, Nigeria, Ethiopia, India or Rwanda)
description: Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) is a global health organization that partners locally and globally to create and scale solutions to the world’s deadliest health threats. Millions of people die from preventable health threats. We collaborate to close the gap between proven, life-saving solutions and the people who need them. Since 2017, we’ve worked with governments and other partners in more than 60 countries to save millions of lives. We work toward a future where people live longer, healthier lives, communities flourish, and economies thrive. This is an ambitious vision, and it inspires us and our partners to make progress every day.   Position Purpose: The Senior Strategist, Data & AI strengthens the capacity of RTSL and its government partners to use data, digital systems, and artificial intelligence to improve public health programs and decision-making. Working across RTSL's program portfolio, the role brings together public health strategy, data architecture, digital transformation, and AI governance to identify high-value opportunities and help translate them into practical, sustainable approaches. The Senior Strategist advises program and country teams on data architecture, interoperability, data governance, and AI readiness; shapes and prioritizes data- and AI-enabled initiatives; and builds RTSL's capacity to use emerging technologies responsibly and effectively. Externally, the role works with governments, technical partners, and the broader global health ecosystem to advance country-owned approaches to stronger data systems and responsible AI. Success in the role means that RTSL and its partners are making better-informed decisions about where and how to invest in data and AI, with stronger underlying data systems, clearer standards and safeguards, and practical applications that deliver measurable public health value. Core Duties and Responsibilities: Data Strategy and Architecture Advise RTSL program and country teams and government partners on strengthening the data foundations needed for effective public health programs, including data architecture, quality, interoperability, metadata, governance, accessibility, and appropriate data use. Ensure teams understand how data flows across systems and identify fragmentation, duplication, quality issues, and other barriers to effective program management and decision-making. Support governments and partners in developing practical, sustainable approaches to data architecture and interoperability that strengthen existing systems and promote country ownership. Translate public health and program needs into clear data requirements and help bridge communication among public health, epidemiology, product, data, and technology teams. Ensure high standards for data quality, usability, interoperability, governance, privacy, and sustainability in collaboration with IT, Legal, and relevant technical teams. Track developments in health information architecture, interoperability standards, digital public goods, analytics, and related fields and assess their implications for RTSL's programs and country partnerships. Applied AI, Innovation, and Responsible Use Shape RTSL's approach to the responsible programmatic use of AI and advanced analytics, ensuring that investments are driven by public health problems and measurable value rather than technology alone. Identify and prioritize high-value opportunities where AI could improve planning, implementation, clinical or public health decision support, analysis, monitoring, or learning -- in close collaboration with program, country, and digital teams. Guide structured assessment of proposed AI use cases, considering the problem to be solved, user and workflow needs, data readiness, feasibility, public health value, equity, privacy, safety, sustainability, and country context. Advise teams on whether to build, buy, adapt, or partner for data- and AI-enabled solutions, emphasizing reuse, interoperability, sustainability, and fit for purpose. Partner with organizational leadership, IT, and Legal to translate RTSL's AI policies and principles into practical guidance and appropriate review processes for programmatic applications. Promote responsible AI practices, including appropriate human oversight, transparency, accountability, privacy, equity, and mechanisms for identifying and responding to risks. Lead responsible experimentation and learning, helping RTSL distinguish promising innovations from approaches that are not sufficiently useful, feasible, or sustainable to pursue. Program Advisory and Organizational Capability Serve as a senior resource to RTSL's program and country teams, helping them integrate data and AI considerations into program design, implementation, monitoring, and scale. Develop practical frameworks, decision aids, guidance, and tools that enable teams to assess data and AI opportunities consistently and rigorously. Build organizational capability in AI and advanced tools through training, coaching, communities of practice, and practical learning opportunities. Help teams develop sufficient AI and data literacy to engage effectively with technical experts, vendors, government counterparts, and partners and make informed decisions. Provide strategic input to digital product and innovation initiatives where broader questions of data architecture, interoperability, AI, or cross-program applicability are relevant, while leaving product ownership and delivery with the responsible technology teams. Capture and share learning from data, digital, and AI initiatives across programs and countries, ensuring that evidence, successes, and failures inform future strategy, investment, and implementation. External Advisory, Partnerships, and Cross-Functional Collaboration Advise government and public health partners on data architecture, interoperability, governance, organizational readiness, and responsible AI adoption in primary health care, epidemic preparedness, and other areas relevant to RTSL's mission. Build relationships with organizations shaping global health data standards, digital public goods, responsible AI, and related technical approaches. Represent RTSL in relevant technical forums and partnerships with governments, funders, multilaterals, academic institutions, technology partners, and peer organizations. Bring external developments and country experience back into RTSL to inform organizational strategy and program design. Work closely with the VP, IT to align programmatic data and AI needs with enterprise technology, cybersecurity, data protection, and infrastructure requirements. Collaborate with Legal and Shared Services on governance, procurement, compliance, contracting, budgeting, and risk management associated with data and AI initiatives. Partner with Development and Communications to support proposals, donor engagement, external communications, and clear articulation of RTSL's approach and learning in public health data and AI. Qualifications:  Experience At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience spanning data, digital health, health information systems, analytics, applied AI, or related areas. Experience working in global public health and with Ministries of Health, national public health institutes, or other government health institutions, preferably across multiple countries. Demonstrated experience working on data architecture and systems, including areas such as interoperability, data standards, metadata, governance, information flows, or data quality. Experience translating complex public health problems into practical data, digital, analytics, or AI approaches. Demonstrated experience operating at the intersection of strategy and implementation and working effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience assessing digital or AI initiatives for feasibility, value, risk, sustainability, and organizational readiness. Experience working with digital products, health information systems, digital public goods, technology vendors, or implementation partners. Experience building organizational capability or supporting adoption of new technologies and ways of working. Experience advising senior government, organizational, or partner stakeholders is strongly preferred.   Skills & abilities Strong public health and systems thinking, with the ability to understand how technology, data, people, workflows, institutions, and policy interact to affect program outcomes. Strong understanding of data architecture, interoperability, data governance, data quality, and the foundations required for effective analytics and AI. Strong working knowledge of responsible AI principles, including privacy, equity, transparency, safety, human oversight, and accountability. Enough technical fluency to engage credibly with data scientists, engineers, architects, and vendors while translating technical issues for public health and organizational leaders. Strong analytical and strategic judgment, including the ability to distinguish promising opportunities from technology-driven solutions without sufficient public health value. Ability to structure ambiguous problems, identify underlying needs, and translate them into practical recommendations and next steps. Excellent facilitation, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills. Ability to work across organizational boundaries and build alignment without direct authority. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex data and technology concepts clearly to government officials, program leaders, donors, and non-technical audiences. Strong cultural awareness and ability to work effectively with partners in diverse and resource-constrained settings. Pragmatic, curious, collaborative, and comfortable working in areas where technology and evidence are evolving rapidly. Education Master's degree or equivalent advanced training in public health, health informatics, digital health, data science, epidemiology, health policy, computer science, information systems, or a related field.   Other Ability to work effectively in a remote, globally distributed organization. Ability and willingness to travel internationally for country engagement, technical consultations, and organizational meetings as needed. Preferred Qualifications Experience in primary health care, cardiovascular health, epidemic preparedness, surveillance, or health systems strengthening. Familiarity with relevant health data and interoperability approaches such as FHIR/HL7, WHO SMART Guidelines and Digital Adaptation Kits, DHIS2, OpenMRS/OpenHIE, and digital public goods. Experience applying AI or advanced analytics to real-world public health or health system problems. Experience working in multilingual and resource-constrained implementation environments. Proficiency in languages in addition to English. Compensation and Benefits: Resolve to Save Lives prides itself on cultivating a supportive, connected remote team doing work that matters. We do everything possible to ensure our employees are connected and set up for success.   The starting salary range for this position in the US is $165,000 to $195,000 annually. The exact offer will be determined by various factors, such as the candidate's skills and experience relative to the requirements of the role.  For applicants based outside the US, salaries are set according to national labor rates for the international NGO sector. In addition to a competitive salary, Resolve to Save Lives provides a generous package of benefits, including:    Health insurance for you and your dependents   Contributions toward retirement    Paid annual leave and sick leave, in addition to public holidays   Two paid, week-long organization-wide breaks at mid-year and end-of-year    Professional development and home office setup benefits   Up-to-date computer equipment      RTSL believes its programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. You will operate as a named member of deal teams under our pod model: paired with Strategic and Enterprise Account Executives, embedded in their weekly cadences, engaged from first discovery through POC, onsite, close, and expansion. Domain coverage. We hire T-shaped practitioners: deep in two to three of the following pillars, conversant and demo-capable across all nine — Governance · Data Governance · Compliance · Risk Management (IT, Security, and Enterprise) · Third-Party Risk Management · Continuous Monitoring · Privacy · Trust · AI Security & Governance. What we're looking for - 5+ years of hands-on GRC experience, with buyer-side depth: you've built, run, or transformed a multi-framework compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, HIPAA/HITRUST, PCI DSS 4.0, GDPR and the US privacy patchwork, NIST CSF 2.0), or advised many organizations doing so. - Working fluency in at least one emerging area — AI governance (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF), GRC engineering / continuous monitoring, or enterprise risk — and genuine curiosity about the rest. - Evidence of customer-facing range: you're credible with a skeptical CISO, a first-time founder, and a procurement team in the same week, and you enjoy the thrill of winning deals. - Production-quality writing: answers, scoping docs, and playbooks that can go to a customer on first draft. - Demonstrated AI fluency: you use LLM tooling in your compliance work today, can judge AI output against authoritative sources, and want to build with it. - Teaching ability: you've trained, presented, published, or enabled others, and you're comfortable building and delivering a session to a large GTM audience. - Sales-process literacy (MEDDPICC or similar), audit-process depth from either side of the table, and the judgment to hold scope boundaries gracefully under deal pressure. title: Principal, EMEA GTM - Physical AI
description: About Nebius: Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The role: Nebius is building the cloud infrastructure that will power the next generation of Physical AI—robotics, autonomous systems, simulation, and embodied intelligence operating in the real world. As a European-headquartered AI infrastructure company, EMEA is a strategic home market for Nebius and one of the most consequential regions in the global Physical AI buildout—from UK autonomy and foundation-model players, to German humanoid and industrial robotics, to Swiss legged-robotics and Israeli/Nordic frontier startups, to the EU's rapidly accelerating defence and dual-use AI ecosystem. The Principal, EMEA GTM – Physical AI owns our GTM motion across EMEA: a regional sales overlay role built to drive repeatable revenue within our first and most important segment—Physical AI natives based in or operating across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. This is not a generalist regional AE seat. It is a domain-led, EMEA-anchored pipeline generator and deal accelerator designed to create leverage: tighter narratives, sharper use-case framing, and category assets that the EMEA field can run independently. You will open strategic, executive-level accounts across the EMEA Physical AI ecosystem, generate qualified pipeline, and personally lead engagement across our EMEA Top 25 target list. On top-tier deals, you will partner directly with EMEA Account Executives, regional sales leadership, and the Physical AI Field CTO team to shape the opportunity early, act as executive sponsor, and accelerate time-to-close. In parallel, you will turn what you learn in-region into repeatable motions—subsegment theses, playbooks, and enablement—tailored to the EMEA buyer, the regulatory environment (EU AI Act, GDPR, data sovereignty), and the region's multi-country go-to-market complexity.
